title: Rivet release scratchpad: safety rivet flow
content:
Context / short goal:
- Purpose: experiment with a low-friction, SLO-driven fractional rollout that nails two problems: (1) fast warmup without oversubscribing GPUs, (2) deterministic escape hatch to pin old model per-tenant if any client-facing regressions appear.
- Persona: release engineer on-call for nightly/quiet window flips; product owner for the feature; partner SRE watching infra.

Non-goals:
- This is NOT a replacement for full canary A/B experiments with large cohorts. Its a tactical safety mechanism for production flips when we need a predictable rollback path.

High-level plan overview:
1) Warmup cohort (0.1% global traffic) for 10m - validate model boot latency, kv-cache population behavior.
2) Progressive fractions: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 60%. Each step is timeboxed and gated on metrics.
3) At any gate failure we revert that cohort and pin affected tenants to previous model version.

Cohort definitions (implementation uses per-tenant sampling key + SDK flag):
- WARMUP: Random sample key mod N = 1 (approx 0.1%)
- STAGE1: sample mod N in [2..11] (1%)
- STAGE2: sample mod N in [12..61] (5%)
- STAGE3: sample mod N in [62..261] (20%)
- GLOBAL: everyone else

Metrics to watch (SLOs & health):
- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 token generation latency (target: p95 < 300ms for average short prompts).
- Error rate: 5xx + 429s, client-side errors (connection resets). Threshold: >0.5% over 5m window = alarm.
- Quality regressions: prompt-check eval pass rate (see quickset below). Drop >2% relative to baseline -> investigate.
- Cost signals: token/sec per GPU and queue depth. If queue depth growth >20% for 10m -> consider throttling next stage.

Gate rules (simplified):
- Proceed to next stage after 20m in current stage AND all metrics within thresholds for last 10m.
- If any threshold breached for 5m, automatically revert that stage (see revert flow).

Pinned rollback semantics (per-tenant):
- When we detect a regression tied to a tenant cohort, we create a tenant pin entry: { tenant_id, pinned_model: v_prev, reason: <short text>, created_by: <engineer> }.
- SDK read path resolves pin before calling routing service; pinned tenants always use pinned_model until removed.
- Pin TTL: manual remove only (to force human review).

Commands / quick operational cheats (internal CLI pseudocode):
- Start warmup: redwood release split apply --model=vX --fraction=0.001 --cohort=WARMUP --note="rivet-warmup-2025-11-03"
- Promote to stage: redwood release split promote --from=WARMUP --to=STAGE1 --min-duration=20m
- Pin tenant: redwood routing pin add --tenant=acme-inc --model=vX --reason="quality-regression-2025-11-03" --author=alex
- Unpin tenant: redwood routing pin remove --tenant=acme-inc --author=priya --ticket=ENG-4312
- Emergency full rollback: redwood release rollback --target-model=vPrev --force --announce-channel=#release-ops

Warmup-specific checks (observability):
- KV-cache heatmap: watch memory growth and hit-rate on prefix-cache for vX. Heat spike >30% relative to baseline -> hold.
- Cold-start P95: if cold-start p95 > 2x baseline, extend warmup by additional 20m.
- Trace sampling: flag 100% of warmup requests for distributed traces to quickly link server-side errors to model code paths.

Quality quickset (small synthetic evals we run continuously during rollout):
- 30 prompt seeds covering hallucination, formatting, and safety (run every 5m against small cohort traffic).
- Baseline pass metric computed from last stable model. Use rolling 1h average.
- Alert rule: relative drop >2% triggers review.

Telemetry & logs to extract if something goes wrong:
- request_id, tenant_id, model_version, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, backend_node_id, kv_cache_hit (bool).
- Pull recent traces for specific tenant IDs when pinning rationale is ambiguous.

Open questions / edge cases to decide before first dry-run:
- Pin ownership: who is responsible for triage and public comms after pin is applied? (ops vs. product)
- Should pin TTL be automated for low-severity regressions? (currently recommended: manual only)
- How to handle mixed-tenant sessions (session touches two tenants with different pins)? Fallback: tie to session owner tenant or force failure on mixed tenancy.

Observations to record during experiment (template):
- time, stage, fraction, manifest_revision, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, eval-pass-rate, notes (any anomalies)

Runbook excerpt (quick):
1) If stage breach -> immediately scale back fraction to previous step and create pin candidates for affected tenants. Notify #release-ops.
2) If infra alarms (GPU OOM, queue explosion) -> abort rollout and call SRE incident per runbook.
3) If quality regressions persist after pinning top 20% of affected tenants -> rollback globally to previous model.

Post-mortem capture fields (if we had to pin/rollback):
- start/stop times, impacted tenants list, trigger metric, root cause hypothesis, mitigation taken, follow-ups.

Nightly dry-run checklist (before silent window):
- [ ] Ensure smoke tests pass against vX in staging (all endpoints).
- [ ] Confirm tracing and eval hooks enabled.
- [ ] Notify stakeholders (#release-ops, product, SRE) with planned start time.
- [ ] Reserve quiet window and ensure on-call coverage.

Next steps (short):
- Align on pin ownership and communication (ask Priya to propose owners).
- Run one dry-run in lower region next Tue 09:30 PT with 0.1% warmup for 30m.
- Add automated playbooks to map observed degraded prompts to offending model diffs (low priority).

Notes to self:
- Keep the pin interface as lightweight as possible — engineers should be able to pin with one CLI command and add minimal context.
- Document all pins in a single Confluence table with links to traces so post-mortems are easier.

References / quick links: ENG-4312 (tracking epic), PR #7890 (routing pin interface), Confluence page "Rivet Release Spec" for design details.

-- alex
